nodes.name: Manual run
nodes.notes: A controller run is requested, not scheduled. The committed panel is research evidence, not a live feed.

nodes.name: Run configuration
nodes.notes: Defaults to the challenger over January 2024. Change model to current, challenger or challenger_v1; change from/to to widen the window. The local CLI remains the batch path for the full 725 mornings.

nodes.name: List session dates
nodes.notes: The dataset decides which mornings exist. A weekend is therefore never requested, and an empty window fails before any model is called.

nodes.name: One item per date
nodes.notes: Each item is handed to the Layer 1 sub-workflow. The configuration fields are copied explicitly so the child never inherits an implicit run state.

nodes.name: Evaluate Layer 1 for each date
nodes.notes: Calls "USD Layer 1 - decision (sub-workflow, controller adapter)" once per date. Replace REPLACE_WITH_LAYER1_SUBWORKFLOW_ID with the imported child workflow id; the placeholder deliberately fails instead of silently calling another workflow.

nodes.name: Summarise decisions
nodes.notes: Aggregates the child decisions with the same hit/miss/flat/no_outcome/no_call tally and Wilson lower bound as backtester/lib/usd_layer1_backtester/backtest_controller.js. A test compares this code with controller.summarise on the real decisions so the two cannot drift.

nodes.name: Report blocked mornings
nodes.notes: Wire to the alert channel. The summary names a block count and the reason codes; no call was invented for a refused morning.

nodes.name: Report complete
nodes.notes: Wire to the research log. Accuracy is gross of costs and is not an edge claim; the receipted count beside it says how many mornings carried a full clock.

parameters.content: Research controller only. It fans out over stored sessions, calls one Layer 1 adapter per morning and publishes an aggregate for inspection. It writes no warehouse row and places no order. The child is model-agnostic: swapping model changes the adapter, not the scoring code.
